chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have dependents, and upon me is a debt, and my condition has become difficult, so teach me a supplication; when I supplicate with it, Allah will grant me sustenance by which I can pay off my debt and assist my dependents with it.'

So he said, 'O servant of Allah! Perform ablution and perfect your ablution, then pray two rak'ahs, completing the bowing and prostration in them, then say: 'O Glorious! O One! O Generous! I turn to You through Muhammad, Your Prophet, the Prophet of Mercy. O Muhammad! O Messenger of Allah! I turn through You to Allah, Your Lord and the Lord of all things, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his Ahl al-Bayt. And I ask You for a breath from Your breaths, and an easy opening, and abundant sustenance, by which I may gather my scattered affairs, pay off my debt, and assist my dependents.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for paying off debt and gaining sustenance according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the 'Salat al-Hajah' (Prayer of Need) as a structured spiritual remedy for financial anxiety, emphasizing the intercessory role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his Ahl al-Bayt. The supplication highlights the Shia theological concept of *tawassul*, where believers seek nearness to Allah through the Prophet's merit to secure *rizq* (sustenance) and alleviate worldly burdens.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Abu Dawood, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I am with dependants, and upon me are debts, and my state has become difficult, so teach me a supplication when I supplicate with it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Grace me what I can payback my debts with, and assist my dependants with it’.

So hesaww said: ‘O servant of Allahsaww! Perform the Wuzu and the extensive Wuzu, then pray two Rak’at of Salāt, completing the Rukū and the Sajdah in them, then say, ‘O Glorious! O One! O Benevolent! I diver to Youazwj by Muhammadsaww Yourazwj Prophetsaww, a Prophetsaww of the Mercy! O Muhammadsaww! O Rasool-Allahsaww! I divert by yousaww to Allahazwj, yoursaww Lordazwj, and the Lordazwj of everything, that Youazwj should Send Blessings upon Muhammadsaww and upon the Peopleasws of hissaww Household, and I ask Youazwj for a gift from Yourazwj gifts, and easy openings, and extensive livelihood I can gather my affairs with, and fulfil my debts with, and assist my dependants with’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn abu Dawud from abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

a man came to the Holy Prophet and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I am a man with (a large) family, indebted; and my condition has become difficult. Please teach me a prayer through which Allah will provide me enough to pay my debts and help my family.’

The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Take Wudu’ properly, then perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer) with complete Ruku‘ and sajdah in both Rak‘at. Thereafter say, “O owner of glory, O the only One, O gracious, I turn to You through Muhammad, Your prophet, the prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, O Messenger of Allah, I have turned through you to Allah, your Lord and the Lord of all things. Allahumma Salli ‘Ala Muhammad wa ‘Ali Muhammad (O Allah grant Muhammad and his family a compensation worthy of their serving Your cause). I appeal to You for relief from that with which You grant relief, an easy success and vast sustenance with which I can overcome my difficulties, pay my debts and help my family.’””
